"PROJECT: IMPOSTER — THE SECRET WORD PARTY GAME

1. YOUR ROLE

Act as a senior full-stack game developer, UI/UX designer, game architect, and software engineer.

Your task is to design and develop a complete, polished, mobile-first party game called IMPOSTER.

The game is inspired by the secret-word social deduction party game.

Do not build just a visual prototype or a static interface. Build a fully functional game with working gameplay mechanics, player management, word distribution, role assignment, voting, scoring, and game settings.

Prioritize clean architecture, excellent user experience, responsive design, and reliable gameplay.

---

2. GAME CONCEPT

IMPOSTER is a social deduction party game designed for 3–12 players playing together in the same physical location.

The game works as follows:

1. Players enter their names.
2. The game randomly selects one player as the Imposter.
3. All normal players receive the same secret word.
4. The Imposter receives no secret word.
5. Players take turns giving clues related to the secret word.
6. Everyone discusses the clues and tries to identify the Imposter.
7. Players vote for the person they suspect.
8. The game reveals the result and determines the winner.

The Imposter must pretend to know the secret word without actually knowing it.

The game should be fun, suspenseful, competitive, and easy to understand.

---

3. GAME MODES

Implement these game modes:

A. Classic Mode

- One randomly selected Imposter.
- Everyone else receives the same secret word.
- Players take turns giving one-word or short-phrase clues.
- After the clue round, players vote.
- Reveal the Imposter.
- Normal players win if they identify the Imposter.
- The Imposter wins if they avoid elimination.

B. Multiple Imposters

- Allow the host to select 1, 2, or 3 Imposters.
- All selected Imposters receive the same Imposter role.
- Normal players receive the secret word.
- Voting must account for multiple Imposters.

C. Timed Mode

- Set a discussion timer.
- Available options: 30 seconds, 60 seconds, 90 seconds, and 120 seconds.
- Automatically move to voting when the timer expires.
- Allow the host to disable the timer.

D. Imposter Guess Mode

After the Imposter is identified, give them one final opportunity to guess the secret word.

- If they guess correctly, the Imposter wins.
- If they guess incorrectly, the normal players win.

Make this feature configurable in settings.

---

4. PLAYER SETUP

Create a player management screen.

Features:

- Minimum players: 3.
- Maximum players: 12.
- Add player names.
- Remove players.
- Edit player names.
- Display all registered players.
- Prevent duplicate names where practical.
- Randomize player order.
- Allow the host to select the number of Imposters.

The interface should make it extremely easy to add players.

Include a prominent START GAME button.

Validate that the number of players is sufficient for the selected number of Imposters.

---

5. WORD SYSTEM

Create a comprehensive word database.

Organize words into categories:

- Animals
- Food
- Countries
- Cities
- Movies
- Sports
- Technology
- Objects
- Professions
- Celebrities
- Nature
- Transportation
- Random Mix

Requirements:

- Each category should contain at least 30 words.
- Allow players to select multiple categories.
- Include a Random category option.
- Avoid repeating recently used words within a session.
- Randomly select one word per round.
- Keep the secret word hidden from unauthorized players.
- Make it easy to add new categories and words in the future.

Include a custom word pack feature so players can create their own word lists.

---

6. ROLE DISTRIBUTION

This is one of the most important parts of the game.

After pressing START GAME:

1. Randomly select the required number of Imposters.
2. Randomly select a secret word.
3. Assign the same secret word to every normal player.
4. Assign the Imposter role to selected players.
5. Never reveal the Imposter's identity to other players d (2D Game, Phone/Tablet)

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

## Objective
- Build a complete, polished, mobile-first IMPOSTER secret-word party game with playable rounds, roles, clues, voting, scoring, and settings.

## Requirements
- Support 3–12 players, 1–3 imposters, configurable discussion timer and imposter word-guess option.
- Include 13 word categories with at least 30 words each, category selection, recent-word avoidance, and custom word packs.
- Use pass-the-phone private role and vote screens; support player add/edit/remove/randomize.
- Deliver a functional game, not a static prototype; use responsive 2D phone/tablet-friendly UI.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them at completion.

## Decisions
- Built as a vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript client-side app with localStorage persistence and no backend.
- Word lists and custom packs are stored in `app.js`; scores, players, settings, and packs persist locally.
- Scoring: normal-player win awards +1 to each non-imposter; imposter win awards +2 to each imposter.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created setup screen with player management, random order, imposter count, timer, guess toggle, category selection, and custom word pack creation.
- Added 13 categories with 30 entries each, word selection avoiding repeats until pool exhaustion, private role reveal, clue round, timed discussion, private voting, result reveal, optional imposter guess, and scoreboard.
- Added responsive styling and captured `screenshots/setup.jpg`.
- `node --check app.js` passed.
- Started local server and opened the app in Playwright.

### Active
- Verify gameplay end-to-end in browser and fix any discovered issues.
- Recheck screenshot after latest CSS adjustments; verify setup fits the 900px viewport.

### Blocked
- Browser automation test failed during a scripted role-deal loop: `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'click')`; determine the correct UI sequence and finish testing.
- Playwright console had a 404 for `/favicon.ico` (non-blocking).

## Next Move
1. Inspect `app.js` gameplay transitions, especially role dealing, voting, and result rendering.
2. Resume browser testing from the current `deal` phase; the prior attempted loop clicked `#revealRole`, `#hideRole`, and `#nextRole` without accounting for rerender timing.
3. Test a complete round through vote tally, imposter guess, score persistence, and play-again behavior.
4. Save/read the latest small JPEG screenshot and run syntax checks; report any remaining assumptions or limitations.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game logic, word database, settings, persistence, rendering, and gameplay transitions.
- `index.html`: App document and shell.
- `styles.css`: Responsive UI and visual design.
- `screenshots/setup.jpg`: Setup-screen capture, taken before the latest CSS edits.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; new files include `app.js`, `index.html`, `styles.css`, and `screenshots/setup.jpg`.

- Playwright last left the page in `deal` phase, round 1, showing the private role screen for Alex.

## Objective
- Build a complete, polished, mobile-first IMPOSTER party game with playable rounds, roles, clues, voting, scoring, and settings.

## Requirements
- Support 3–12 players, 1–3 imposters, configurable discussion timer, and optional imposter word guess.
- Include 13 categories with at least 30 words each, category selection, recent-word avoidance, and custom word packs.
- Use pass-the-phone private role and vote screens; support player add/edit/remove/randomize.
- Deliver a functional responsive 2D game; make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript client-side app with localStorage; no backend.
- Scores, players, settings, and custom packs persist locally.
- Scoring: normal-player win awards +1 to each non-imposter; imposter win awards +2 to each imposter.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented setup, player management, settings, categories/custom packs, role reveal, clue round, discussion timer, private voting, results, scoring, and replay flow.
- Fixed role-deal progression: after hiding a revealed role, the player can still pass the phone; guarded the reveal handler when its button is absent.
- `node --check app.js` passes; browser test reached results without page errors.

### Active
- Fix word selection: browser testing found `state.word` becomes the entire category string (e.g. all of “Random Mix”) rather than one word.
- Complete end-to-end testing after fixing word selection, including final guess correctness, score persistence, and play-again behavior.
- Recheck setup layout and capture a setup screenshot; latest `screenshots/setup.jpg` may instead show a gameplay screen.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Update `wordsFor` or `startGame` in `app.js` so category strings become arrays of individual words before pooling and random selection.
2. Repeat browser testing through role deal, clues, voting, guess, results, persistence, and replay.
3. Verify `screenshots/setup.jpg` shows setup and rerun syntax checks.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game logic, word lists, persistence, rendering, and gameplay transitions.
- `index.html`: App document and shell.
- `styles.css`: Responsive styling.
- `screenshots/setup.jpg`: Setup-screen capture; verify it is current.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Local server is at `http://localhost:3002`.
- `WORDS` values are comma-separated strings; current `wordsFor(category)` returns the string unchanged, so `flatMap(wordsFor)` pools each full category as one “word.”
- Automated test script is at `/tmp/opencode/test-game.cjs`; its guess input hit the 50-character limit while trying to enter the full category string, confirming the word-selection bug.
